lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: The date of birth and nationality should not be on the résumé.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary for U.S. applications and can create privacy or bias risks.

items.says: Make the portfolio link clearly clickable and identifiable.
Link directly to relevant case studies, if available.
Add a LinkedIn link if you maintain one.
Move Education below Experience and Projects.
items.because: With several years of relevant experience, your work is the stronger opening evidence.

items.says: Add the A/B test sample size or test volume and clarify how abandonment was measured.
Do not imply the A/B test established a definitive effect if the result was not statistically significant.
A 3:1 contrast ratio is not the general WCAG AA threshold for body text.
items.because: Normal text generally requires 4.5:1; 3:1 applies to large text.

items.says: Meeting a contrast threshold alone does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA conformance for a design system.
items.because: Broader conformance requires assessment across the applicable criteria.

items.says: Fix the present-participle opening to match the completed role.
Clarify what changed based on the findings rather than making the call reduction sound like a direct result of synthesis.
Clarify how the 23% reduction was measured and give its before-and-after period.
Clarify what “the top five” refers to and whether the fixes shipped in the same release cycle.
Indicate the scope or result of the shipped fixes if possible.
items.because: The bullet currently relies only on the number adopted.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period behind “doubled.”
Say whether the additional tests were completed or used in decisions, if supported.
items.because: The current wording does not distinguish those outcomes from tests merely initiated.

items.says: Clarify the measurement window and, if available, the number of customers or sign-ups behind the percentages.
Make sure completed sign-ups were measured consistently before and after launch.
The stated average recommendation rating is not Net Promoter Score.
items.because: NPS is calculated from the proportions of promoters and detractors; 6.1 to 8.4 sounds like an average rating.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period for the reported change.
Avoid implying the research alone caused the change unless that attribution is supported.
Add the time period or appointment volume behind the missed-appointment rates, if available.
Keep the claimed effect of the reminder proportionate to the evidence.
Change the present tense to match the completed role.
Clarify whether the setup times are typical values or averages, if known.
Add the measurement period or call-volume basis for the 30% reduction, if available.
Define an age range for “older patients” if it was part of the study criteria.
items.because: An age range would be more precise.

items.says: The first project bullet overlaps with the following outcome bullets.
items.because: Use the space to distinguish your contribution or the deliverable from the measured results.

items.says: The change from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33.3% reduction, not a 50% improvement.
The change from 65% to 85% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
Do not repeat audio landmarks and high-contrast colors as if they were separate evidence.
items.because: The same intervention appears in both outcome bullets.

items.says: Do not imply the results generalize beyond the study.
Clarify the period and booking volume supporting the drop in phone bookings.
Avoid implying the redesign caused the entire decrease without evidence for that connection.
Specify whether the six issues were the most serious, all issues found, or those blocking task completion.
items.because: “Fixing the six issues” leaves their scope unclear.

items.says: If available, clarify what later teams used the handbook to do beyond adding Spanish-language booking.
“interveiws” is misspelled.
Organize Skills so methods and tools are easy to scan separately.
Include other relevant platforms or analysis tools only if you have used them and can discuss them.
The Skills section is brief compared with the experience bullets.
